# Verify and fix

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

Verify maps every v0 acceptance line in `spec.md` to a test or a browser check and reports pass, fail, or missing. that is `python` on Windows and `python3` elsewhere, with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and `-X utf8`. The spec folder command includes `--root docs/specs`. A bug in work that is already shipping is not this page: that is [`$crav1-fix-bug`](from-fix-bug.md).

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-verify-build-against-spec
@docs/specs/<slug>/
```

A verify rerun checks again only the tasks whose branch or tip moved since the last verify, and says which rows it kept, for example `Kept from the last verify: T1, T3 (branch and tip unchanged).` When spec.md, plan.md or tasks.md changed, every row is checked again. Rows are written by `scripts/verify_rows.py set --file docs/specs/orders-api/verify.md --task T6 --status "Implemented, verified" --evidence "tests pass" --yes`.

## Steps

| Step | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verify | — | Reads `spec.md`, `tasks.md`, `plan.md`, and the running tree. The spec folder is the one you @-mention, or the one folder the resolver prints (`orders 1.0` matches `orders-1-0`, then one unique playbook, title, or work-item name, then one unique ordered token subsequence such as `cc 1.0` for `cc-process-1-0`). Several matches are listed and the run stops. No match lists the nearest slugs. It does not pick the most recently edited tree. Leads with a TL;DR: which tasks are implemented and verified, which are tick pending, which are not, and acceptance lines with no task. Then the details in `verify.md`. Ends by naming the next command |
| Read the result | Decide: fix, build more, tick, or ship | Each task is implemented and verified, implemented and verified with the tick still open, implemented but verify failed, not implemented, or claimed done but unverified. Wiring gaps are numbered `G#`. A task that is not implemented goes back to [Build tasks](from-plan-to-build.md), not to fix. A tick-pending gap is not that path |
| Fix | `$crav1-fix-build-gaps`, or name a gap `G#` | Takes one gap in order: failed, then unverified, then `G#`. Omit the gap to take the next. Makes the smallest fix inside the spec, appends to `fix-log.md`, and updates that one `verify.md` row |
| Live wiring | `$crav1-fix-build-gaps` when the gap is a live path (ports, proxy, SQL, an unpublished URL) | Same queue and same writes as fix-build-gaps, preferring live or untested wiring rows. When the fix changes how the parts connect, asks once whether to run `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` and does not run it |
| Prove again | `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec` | Re-runs the matrix |

On a base branch (`main`, `develop`, the `Merges into` branch, `release/*`) `$crav1-fix-build-gaps` edits no code: it first offers **Create fix/<slug> from <into> (Recommended)**, an existing branch, or stop. A typed branch name is that card's free-text answer, hint `Type a branch name`. A headless run stops unless it has `new-branch`.

When `$crav1-build-walk` opened `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec`, the case line is not the Next line.

## Local test dependencies

- **Start it.** The kit starts it with the repo's documented command, or a sensible default such as `azurite` or `docker compose up -d <service>`, and checks it answers.
- **Skip the tests that need it.** The rest run. `verify.md` lists the skipped tests under **Skipped tests**, with the dependency and why.
- **Stop.** No tests run.

A run with no window writes the question to the two-pass questions file in the system temp folder and puts the missing dependency at the top of the summary as a `BLOCKER:` line, not a footnote. When tests skip anyway for a dependency the check missed, for example "5 skipped because Azurite wasn't running", the kit treats it the same way. A worker returns `STATUS: needs_dependency` and the orchestrator asks.

## Tick pending (1.136.0)

When the evidence passed, the `tasks.md` row is still `[ ]`, and the pull request is recorded merged, the status is **Implemented, verified, tick pending**. `verify.md` has no `Next:` line.

## What gets written

- `docs/specs/<slug>/verify.md`: the acceptance matrix, plus **Skipped tests** when you chose skip for a missing dependency. the TL;DR includes **Implemented, verified, tick pending**. the Tasks overview has one row per T# in `tasks.md`; a row for a T# that `tasks.md` does not have is dropped and the reply names it, so the ready check's `**Catch up first**` block needs only this command for both a behind task and a stray row.
- One `[x]` on a tick-pending row in `tasks.md`, only after you say yes.

## The reply (1.168.0)

The chat reply is brief: `Verify — <slug>`, the counts on one `Result:` line, one line per task whose state changed since the last verify (for example `T6 failed: 4 cursor tests fail at the PR's tip` or `T44 row dropped: not in tasks.md`), then `Run next:`, Waiting and `Report: docs/specs/<slug>/verify.md`. Run next opens with **Catch up first** when something can be settled now: a plan note goes to `$crav1-tighten-plan`, and an uncommitted `verify.md` gets `$crav1-finalize-commit` and then `git push`. Say `full` to see the TL;DR and the Tasks overview in chat; they are always in `verify.md`.

- `docs/specs/<slug>/fix-log.md`: one entry per gap, with the fix and the re-proof.
- The smallest code fix for that gap.

Not written: `spec.md`, unimplemented tasks. Verify does not run `$crav1-fix-bug` or `$crav1-review-pr`.

## Merged across branches (1.64.0)

When the spec's work sits on several branches, `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec` adds a Branches line to the TL;DR, for example `Branches: 1 of 3 merged into develop. Not merged: feat/orders-retry (2 commits), feature/orders-export (3 commits).` The base is the repo's `Merges into` branch, else the default branch.

- **Merged** means the branch is in its base, its commits are there as the same change, or a merged PR shows on GitHub or Azure DevOps (only when `gh` or `az` is already signed in). A deleted branch whose work is in the base is `merged, branch deleted`.
- **Rewritten** branches say `branch rewritten since last read`; nothing errors.
- A branch two specs share is listed under each with `(also in <slug>)`.
- "Demoable" needs every branch merged. Otherwise: `built and verified, not merged yet`, next `$crav1-open-pr` or `$crav1-merge-pr`; a branch that already has a pull request is named, for example `$crav1-open-pr` to push to PR 77 and update its description or comment. `$crav1-open-pr` proposes the base `develop` here (into, then Merges into, then default), and `$crav1-review-pr` finds the spec the same way. After a merge, `$crav1-merge-pr` says `2 of 3 branches of orders now merged into develop`. `$crav1-help status orders` shows the same line, and `$crav1-ado-sync` suggest-features counts unmerged branches as open work.
- Nothing writes `Status:`. It is report only. Refs on disk; nothing fetches.

## Host setup tasks (1.115.0)

A `(host setup)` task passes only when its script's `check` part, run now against the live host, prints `ok` for every setting. Verify never applies the script.

`$crav1-verify-build-against-spec` reads the branch line, a sub-branch, promotion, a tick-pending row, a host-setup task, and the one next line only when that case applies.

## After

Reference pages: [verify-build-against-spec](reference/skills/crav1-verify-build-against-spec.md) · [fix-build-gaps](reference/skills/crav1-fix-build-gaps.md) · [fix-build-gaps](reference/skills/crav1-fix-build-gaps.md)

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: Run next, never a `Next:` line. `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked.

The ready check says `verified on feat/orders-readme, waits for PR 71 to merge`, and the row becomes **Implemented, verified, tick pending** once the merge is recorded. `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec` writes it.

there is one wording for evidence that passed while the row is still `[ ]`: `Implemented, verified, tick pending`, whether the branch is still waiting for its merge or the merge is recorded. The older `Implemented, verified on branch` is still read and is rewritten once when the row script next writes the file. Writing one row no longer moves the whole-file `Spec stamp:`, so rows that were not checked again still rerun after a spec change; the last row of a full verify passes `--all-rows` to move it.

## 1.198.0 changes

When a test dependency is down, `$crav1-verify-build-against-spec` runs `scripts/dep_check.py containers --service <name>` first: a stopped docker or podman container, or a stopped podman machine, gets its start commands (`podman machine start`, `podman start <name>`), and an install is offered only when no runtime or container exists.
